newsitem.title: MALI: Mali rice buyer plans own production to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Mali rice buyer plans own production to cut costs.

text.p: Private Malian rice buyer Societe des Rizeries du Mali (SERIMA) plans to cut rice costs and secure supplies by setting up its own paddies, the company's managing director told Reuters.

"By producing ourselves, a tonne of rice will cost us 70,000 CFA (francs) against 110,000 CFA at the moment from farmers, which will put us in a better competitive position against imports," Managing Director Aliou Boubacar said in an interview, estimating rice cost savings to the company at 30 percent.
The company currently buys directly from farmers.
"We have obtained agreement in principle for purchase of 10,000 hectares and our objective in the long term is 20,000 hectares," he said this week.
A delegation including SERIMA and Mali'S Ministry for Rural Development recently completed a fact-finding mission to Brazil's largest rice grower, CODEVASF, he said.

The company also aims to export rice to neighbouring Ivory Coast by developing technology to meet demand there for smoked rice. Ivory Coast has said it aims to be self-sufficient in rice by 2000 but still imports 300,000 tonnes a year, close to 50 percent of its annual consumption.
Technical experts from CODEVASF's studies unit MAGNA would visit Mali in the next few weeks to advise on setting up rice production, he added.

SERIMA was set up as an industrial rice producer in 1996 and bought four price paddies recently privatised by the state Office du Niger (ON) -- Mali's largest rice grower with production of 250,000 tonnes a year from 53,000 hectares.
